title: Transforming subcellular spatial transcriptomics: deep learning models for cell segmentation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Retrieved the full article text from the PubMed Central page (PMC13490946) and read its data availability statement verbatim: 'No datasets were generated or analyzed in support of this review.' Also read the paper's only table (Table 1) in full, and checked Europe PMC metadata: pubTypeList = ['research-article','Review','Journal Article'], hasSuppl = 'N'. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint returned a 297-byte non-zip response, i.e. no supplement exists. No accession numbers were found anywhere in the text (the only 'accessions' text-mined were arXiv DOIs of cited methods papers), and a DOI search of Zenodo/Dryad returned nothing.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The descriptive contents of Table 1 (nine segmentation models with their architecture class, input/output formats, intended application, evaluation metric names and GPU requirement). I did not verify any of those model properties independently, and the table contains no performance numbers at all, so there is nothing numeric in this paper to check against files.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. The paper is a narrative review and states explicitly in its data availability section: 'No datasets were generated or analyzed in support of this review.' No supplementary files (Europe PMC hasSuppl = N, supplementaryFiles endpoint returns no archive), no accessions, no repository deposit. Nothing to download, so A1 fails and scoring stops here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed beyond A1: with no data file there is no column of any kind. The only table is a qualitative feature comparison of nine published tools (architecture class, input format, 'best suited for'), with no measured outcome and no performance values.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not assessed; no data. Any segmentation project would have to obtain images and transcript coordinates from third-party spatial transcriptomics datasets that this paper neither hosts nor indexes.

a4_units_stated.note: Not assessed; no measurements are reported anywhere in the paper, so there are no units to state.

a5_enough_rows.note: The only machine-readable content is Table 1, which has nine rows (one per reviewed model). That is three orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row threshold, and the rows are tool descriptions, not labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Moot, but worth recording: Table 1 lists a GPU (graphics processing unit) as required or recommended for every one of the nine reviewed models, so the task this review covers is not a CPU-laptop task even if data were assembled.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: the paper reports no counts for any dataset.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessed; no label exists. Note for any derived project: cell segmentation 'ground truth' in this field is usually either hand-drawn annotation or another segmentation model's output, which is exactly the circularity A8 warns about.

existing_models.name: Cellpose (versions 1-3) and Cellpose-SAM, open-source deep learning cell segmentation tools (SAM = Segment Anything Model, a general image-segmentation foundation model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verifiable from this paper: the review's Table 1 lists only the metric names used (average precision, true/false positives and negatives, 'human-consensus bound') and reports no numbers or splits. The review's text states Cellpose-SAM performs close to an estimated human-consensus upper bound.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The review names the unsolved parts as generalisation across tissues and resolutions, large training-data requirements and high compute cost for transformer and foundation-model approaches.

existing_models.name: BIDCell and UCS, convolutional network segmenters that use transcript maps plus nuclear stain images
existing_models.score_and_split: No numbers given in this review; Table 1 records only that BIDCell is evaluated with the CellSPA framework and UCS with cell number, transcript count and cell area.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transcript-to-cell assignment accuracy across platforms; both are listed as needing a CUDA-enabled NVIDIA GPU for training.

existing_models.name: SCS (Subcellular Spatial transcriptomics Cell Segmentation), a transformer-based spot-to-cell assignment model
existing_models.score_and_split: No numbers in this review; Table 1 says only 'compared with other segmentation methods'.

existing_models.name: CellSAM and CellViT++, foundation-model segmenters for microscopy and pathology images
existing_models.score_and_split: No numbers in this review; metric names only (precision, recall, F1, mean average precision, panoptic quality).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Compute cost and limited availability of pretrained models for specific biological applications, per the review's discussion.

backbone.name: Cellpose-SAM / CellSAM (Segment Anything Model derivatives for cell images)
backbone.hardware: Table 1 of the review lists a CUDA-enabled NVIDIA graphics processing unit as required for every foundation-model entry; image segmentation inference over whole tissue sections is not a 16 GB CPU-laptop job.
backbone.licence: Not stated in this paper; Cellpose is distributed under a permissive open-source licence, but I did not verify licences for the other tools.

integration.partner_dataset: None available through this paper. A derived project would need third-party data such as 10x Genomics Xenium or Vizgen MERSCOPE public releases, which this review neither hosts nor lists accessions for.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper's contents, because the paper contains no identifiers, coordinates or measurements to join to anything.

controls.positive_control: None possible: no data in which a known signal could be recovered.
controls.negative_control: None possible: there is no label to shuffle and no feature matrix to ablate.
controls.external_validation: Not applicable. Independent segmentation benchmarks on serial tissue sections were published in 2025 (Nature Communications s41467-025-64292-3 and s41467-025-64990-y; Nature Methods s41592-025-02617-2, found by search), but they are separate studies, not validation sets for anything in this paper.

honest_claim_h3: No claim can be made from this paper's data because it has none; any segmentation model built around this topic would be claiming accuracy on tissues and platforms represented in somebody else's public spatial transcriptomics release, judged against human-drawn or model-derived masks rather than a physical measurement of cell boundaries.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tissue images plus RNA molecule positions to predict which cell each RNA molecule belongs to.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would need microscopy images and the coordinates of individual RNA (ribonucleic acid) molecules from subcellular spatial transcriptomics experiments, with hand-drawn cell outlines as the answer key. This paper supplies none of that: its only table has 9 rows, each describing a published software tool.
plain_idea.predict: A mask marking the boundary of every cell, or equivalently an assignment of each RNA molecule to one cell. The true answer normally comes from manual annotation of images by a person, or from a nuclear stain expanded by a rule, neither of which is a direct measurement of where the cell membrane is.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Better segmentation would change every downstream conclusion in spatial transcriptomics, because wrongly assigned RNA molecules create cells that look like mixtures of two cell types. But that payoff belongs to projects built on real image data, not on this review.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes zero data; its data availability statement says no datasets were generated or analysed. Any data would have to come from third-party releases that the reviewed models were already trained and tested on, so we would have strictly less, not more.

confidence_score.why: Calibrated per-cell confidence would need repeated independent annotations of the same cells to estimate annotator noise. Nothing in this paper provides replicates, and the review reports no agreement statistics beyond mentioning a 'human-consensus bound' for Cellpose-SAM without a number.

models_beatable.why: The named incumbents are 2024-2025 foundation-model segmenters (Cellpose-SAM, CellSAM, CellViT++) with open code and an active benchmarking literature; three independent platform-and-segmentation benchmarks appeared in Nature Communications and Nature Methods in 2025. That is a field with recent models and honest external evaluation already in progress.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Every condition fails: there is no dataset here to add to a baseline, no join key, and the existing models were evaluated on data this paper does not contain, so no shared split exists.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The only conceivable project - assemble public Xenium/MERSCOPE/CosMx sections and re-evaluate the nine reviewed segmenters on a common held-out-tissue split - would draw all of its data from other papers, needs a GPU (graphics processing unit) for every model in the review's own Table 1, and duplicates three segmentation benchmarks already published in 2025.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible because there is no dataset. The one firm fact is from the paper's own Table 1: a CUDA-enabled NVIDIA graphics processing unit is listed as required or recommended for all nine reviewed models, which rules out the 16 GB CPU-only laptop constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the data availability statement, which took one page fetch: 'No datasets were generated or analyzed in support of this review.' That single sentence kills it.

verdict_reason: Narrative review with no data at all - the paper states outright that no datasets were generated or analysed, Europe PMC confirms no supplementary files and no accessions, and the only table is a nine-row qualitative comparison of published tools containing no performance numbers. Part A1 fails, and even the derived project (re-benchmarking cell segmentation tools) would need a graphics processing unit per the paper's own Table 1 and would re-tread three 2025 benchmark papers.
